about: Data only. What each compression_level of FFmpeg's FLAC encoder sets, per release tag. Read from the history of libavcodec/flacenc.c; no code or comments copied. Not yet confirmed against reference files of each release.

source.read_under: CLAUDE.md, the paragraph on an encoder's settings table per release (lead, 2026-11-23): read by one agent, who writes no analyzer code
also_read: libavcodec/flacdata.c and libavcodec/flac.h (block size table and limits)
libavcodec/lpc.c (only its blob id per tag is recorded; its algorithms were not read)
source.commit_fields: tag_commit is the commit the tag points to; read_from_commit is the last commit before the tag that changed the file, and file_blob is the git blob read

level_table_note: The table never changed between v0.5 and n8.0.1 in this file. What changed is how a revision applies it and which options override it (see revisions).

log_search.note: each step evaluates the best order so far and the orders one step below and above it, within min to max

block_size.rule: The block size is the largest standard FLAC block size (192, 576, 1152, 2304, 4608, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768) that does not exceed floor(sample rate x block_time_ms / 1000), and 192 where none does. The frame_size option, 16 to 65535, replaces it.

order_candidates_rules.plain: Candidate orders of 2level, 4level and 8level are evenly spaced up to one step above the maximum order (orders counted from 1: the spacing formula reaches maximum order plus 1 for the top candidate when the minimum is 1); a candidate below the first order becomes the first order; no duplicates are skipped.
order_candidates_rules.distinct_clipped: Same spacing, with each candidate clipped into the minimum to maximum order range and a candidate equal to the previous one skipped. The two rules differ in the top candidate of levels 6 and 8 (see candidate_orders_* in levels): the plain rule names an order one above the maximum, the distinct_clipped rule names the maximum.

settings.option_defaults: all of these are unset (-1, or 0 for lpc_coeff_precision and frame_size) and then take the level value or the defaults below
settings.lpc_coeff_precision: 15 unless set to 1 to 15 (above 15 is an error; 0 means unset)
settings.stereo: adaptive per frame for two channels, independent otherwise; no option to force a mode

unsettled.item: LPC analysis in libavcodec/lpc.c (window function, how the estimation search method picks an order, coefficient quantization, effective precision after quantization) was not read; each revision lists the lpc.c blob ids of its tags so a change there can be spotted.

unsettled.scope: revisions with the plain order candidate rule
unsettled.item: For levels 6 and 8 the top candidate is one above the level's maximum order (9 and 13); the order search of these revisions then used coefficients that lpc.c computes only up to the maximum order. Whether frames of that order occur in files is for the reference files to settle.
No table value was confirmed against reference files of its release; the next step is encoding with each release and reading the parameters back.

Values that depend on the audio, not on the level: frames shorter than the maximum order or shorter than 5 samples use fixed or verbatim coding; partition orders are clamped by block size and predictor order; the short last frame; constant subframes; wasted bits. They are file facts to settle with reference files.
Command line programs (fftools) were not read; a release could pass compression_level or frame_size on its own.
Options come from the generic codec context, so which spelling a command line accepted (use_lpc, not lpc_type) follows options.c of that tag, which was only spot-checked.
lpc_passes defaults to -1 here and lpc.c of that tag does not replace it; no level uses cholesky, so no level value is affected.
Settings are read both from private options and, in a compatibility block, from the generic codec context; which of the two a command line reached was not traced.
The partition order search does not treat equal minimum and maximum partition orders specially, unlike its neighbors r22 and r24; the effect on levels 0 and 1 (both 2) was not traced.
Tags on release branches carry backports, so a release branch can hold a revision that master gets later; the releases list gives the revision per tag. Snapshots between tags are not covered.
32-bit input and sample rates not in the standard list are handled differently from earlier releases; the level table is unaffected, the stored header values were not read.
